governance.attested_by: run158 endogenous West/Panhandle Waha collapse-frequency on the run157 recipe (gap G6) 2026-06-25
governance.note: PROBE (not a keeper). run158 = the CURRENT ERCOT keeper recipe (run157: run134/run155a base + measured DAM-AS scarcity overlay from 2024, RTORDPA overlay, storage-AS-from-2024, load-RRS-from-2023, STGAS net-load drag OFF, West/Panhandle net-load Waha delivered-gas step with delivered floor $0.40, oil-primary CT binning, coal-PRB passthrough sigmoid floor 0.78, ST_GAS committed offer delta 0.0) re-solved on current main with ONE change: the two-regime Waha SPLIT FREQUENCY made ENDOGENOUS (ercot_west_gas_endogenous_collapse, env ERCOT_WEST_ENDOGENOUS_COLLAPSE=1), closing the last measured input of the West net-load gas shape (gap G6). Previously the split between the collapsed (deep-negative, low-net-load) and firm (high-net-load) regime was set by the MEASURED Waha negative-price-day frequency (data/raw/ercot_zonal_gas_hub.csv neg_day_freq; 2024 EIA-authoritative 0.42, 2023 0.03, 2025 0.11). It is now derived from FORECAST West/Panhandle oversupply: the fraction of hours West+Panhandle wind+solar generation exceeds local West load plus the region's export takeaway (WESTEX 10.0 GW + PNHNDL 2.68 GW), via fuel.ercot_west_oversupply_collapse_freq, consumed at the run_calibration call site from the same per-zone VRE capacity x CF, load, and transmission topology the model already builds. Every input is a forecast quantity, so the frequency regenerates for any forward year and responds to changed conditions (more West VRE -> more oversupply hours -> higher collapse frequency; unit-tested). The annual-mean Waha basis set by apply_ercot_zonal_gas_basis is still preserved exactly (only redistributed across hours), the deep value still forced by mean-preservation and floored at the physical burner-tip delivered minimum ($0.40), the firm level still the cited firm Waha delivered basis (HH-0.50) - none tuned to a price or volume residual. The measured neg_day_freq is NOT used in this run; it is retained only as the backcast realization, logged alongside the endogenous value on every solve for validation, never re-pinned. All other levers are run157's, inherited unchanged and tracing to measured inputs (CAMPD net-load-filtered outage windows, measured ERCOT 60-Day DAM AS series + storage up-AS reservation + load-resource RRS-UFR credit driving the energy+reserve co-opt, measured RTORDPA + DAM-AS reliability overlays, measured F923/Henry-Hub fuel prices, EIA-860 BTM CHP host steam, Laredo West->South zone correction). No unit pinned to its observed CEMS generation; no input rescaled so the model output lands on actuals.
governance.residuals_note: VALIDATION (endogenous vs measured collapse frequency, the central result of this probe): endogenous West-oversupply frequency 0.017 / 0.003 / 0.006 vs measured Waha neg-day 0.030 / 0.420 / 0.110 for 2023 / 2024 / 2025 (in-run, on the dispatched demand+VRE; 2024/2025 clamped up to the 0.01 minimum). The power-oversupply proxy tracks the measured frequency in 2023 (0.017 vs 0.030) but is near-zero in 2024/2025 because West local load plus the 12.68 GW WESTEX+PNHNDL takeaway absorbs essentially all West VRE, so genuine West *power* oversupply almost never occurs. The measured 2024 record (0.42) and 2025 (0.11) were driven by Permian *gas-pipeline takeaway* constraints (associated-gas glut vs constrained interstate capacity), a DIFFERENT physical phenomenon than power oversupply and a measured *outcome* with no forward analogue (CLAUDE.md #12) - so the proxy correctly does not reproduce it. ISOLATED EFFECT OF THE LEVER (documented, kept per #1/#11, NOT fit away): with the collapse regime now ~1% of hours instead of the measured 42% in 2024, the 48 West/Panhandle gas units see firm Waha (~HH-0.50) in ~99% of hours, so the West CTs (Morgan Creek, Permian, Ector, Topaz) idle rather than running cheap collapse-hour baseload. run158 CT_PEAKER model/EIA-923: 5.90/7.56 (2023, -22.0%), 5.22/8.21 (2024, -36.4%), 5.00/7.11 (2025, -29.7%) - the West-CT under-run deepens vs the measured-collapse keeper, which is the honest forward consequence of removing a measured input that had no forward analogue (the West/Permian CTs serve large local load and are not transmission-closable, per the run154 Far_West-split rejection). This is the open root cause, never closed by reverting to the measured frequency. DETERMINATION NOT-YET, undocumented out-of-tolerance: (1) fuelmix C1 2024 ST_GAS -8.85 TWh / -1.9pp - ST_GAS gas-steam under-production with run157's STGAS-drag OFF recipe on current main (the net-load reliability-drag floor that holds ST_GAS online is deliberately off in run157's lineage); (2) sysvol C2 2025 gas -6.4%; (3) price_mean C3a 2024 +9.6% and price_shape C3b 2023 NRMSE 0.310 / 2024 0.208 - the energy-only-dual price-level/shape limitation inherited from run151/run157. These are recorded as MODEL MISS / inherited structural limitations of the run157 recipe on current main, not closed by a gas-side fit. run158 is a PROBE demonstrating the endogenous collapse-frequency mechanism (gap G6 closed) on the keeper recipe; it is not promoted to keeper.
